items.statement: Line complications requiring hospital contact vary more between home care arrangements (agency team, visit frequency, living alone) than between PICC and midline once antibiotic and duration are accounted for.
items.rationale: Variation between nursing teams (c2) and the agency difference in the explanatory study (c3) suggest care arrangements matter; the local cohort can test it.
items.risks: Undercounting home-managed events if agency notes are not shared; confounding by line choice.

items.statement: Patients and carers who receive demonstration teaching report line problems earlier than those who receive a leaflet.
items.rationale: Teaching method was linked to knowledge in an undated evaluation, and delayed reporting appears in patient accounts.
items.risks: Teaching method is not recorded in the OPAT database.

items.statement: Most complications occur in the first three weeks, so a week-two review would catch most failing lines.
items.rationale: Timing reported in the three-centre review (c1).
items.risks: Timing depends on when problems reach hospital records.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 frames the quantitative strand and the interview sampling.
